column8: Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 reservoir: the measured anchor for any AI sentence (posts down about a sixth in a year against a control); say its basis each time (one freelance platform, short remote jobs, posts to July 2023), never as illustrators' income or Laura's.
Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 store: the effect widened with time and a placebo is near zero, so structural in the plain sense; pairs with row 1, one platform.

Wed 18 Nov: store: sizes differ by version (3.7%/9.4% in 2023, 2.1%/5.2% in 2025, 1.9% to 17.0% by specification), so quote only that every version is negative, or name the version with its figure; never 9.4% alone.

Wed 18 Nov: store: true of Upwork image freelancers, but the use column maps it onto Laura; say above-median platform earners lost more, never that bestselling is no shield for her, and set rows 10-11 beside it.
Wed 18 Nov: the authors' own reading of their data in an opinion piece, no new data; the widening rests on row 2's measured growth.
Wed 18 Nov: store for claim 2: name the version (revised July 2026, accepted QJE) with its figures and say non-AI sales, not the sales rate (3% or 5%); the May 2025 text gives other figures.
Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 reservoir for claim 2: the human work that survives is the work a machine copies badly or cannot legally sign for; stock images, and quality is a model proxy.
Wed 18 Nov: store: text AI on one platform; supports the shortest, most generic commissions going first, never a measure of image models.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the honest counter-case (orders and revenue up on cheaper anime commissions); five months, cheap personal orders, one platform; keeps any AI sentence from reading one-way.

Wed 18 Nov: store: 97.41% to artists registered before the leak says little when nearly every artist was registered before it (no pre-leak share given); use only that commercial orders stayed roughly stable, never that established names kept the paying work.
Wed 18 Nov: store for claim 2: the escape route runs up the ladder of difficulty; logo contests, abstract and university summary only.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 reservoir for claim 2: after the 2023 ruling AI-art gigs sold for about a third less, so copyright has a price that a human author's pages carry; abstract and highlights only, one platform.

Wed 18 Nov: store: the first union-scale count (26% of UK illustrators had lost work, Jan 2024, 787 replies, self-selected); quote the loss only, never the 78% expectation (a fear question, row 19) or decreased in value as a measured fall.

Wed 18 Nov: store: 46% (2026, 549 replies) confirmed in a secondary report; the 32% came from a separate, far larger self-selected sample, so never rose 14 points as a trend; give 46% with its basis, or both with their samples.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e reservoir: a secondary report leaves the 22%'s base unclear (all respondents or those whose income fell), so confirm it before one in five; mixed causes; never set beside the 73.9% as if the deposit were a year of illustration income (case l.44-45 names advances, speaking, licensing); Q56-035 made the same pairing on US top-author data.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 Client Knowledge: Laura is a graphic novelist (case l.13), so lead with comics and graphic novels at 56% (above children's books) and give children's books' 42% beside it, never the 42% alone; commissioned work, overlapping areas, 549 replies.
Wed 18 Nov: store: AI shows up in briefs, fees and turnaround, not only in lost jobs; UK commissioned illustrators, self-reported.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 reservoir: the largest survey, with its basis (24,991 creators in Japan, Sep-Oct 2025; about one in eight report an AI income cut); the 12.0% is all creators, never illustrators alone (the occupation split was not reached).
Wed 18 Nov: presentation guard for any AI sentence: quote loss questions, never fear ones (88.6% fear against 12.0% loss, about 7 to 1, Keel arithmetic checked); one survey.

Wed 18 Nov: keep the rule (say measurably fallen, never one percentage for illustrators' income) and drop the 2-17% range, which leaves out row 6's larger falls (non-AI artists -29%) and row 3's -17.0% income specification.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 aha candidate: her career has its own risk as well as the market's, and the plan meets both by owning promises first; the S&P figures match the repo's Damodaran file (85.4% checked), but never splice SoA's 26% and AOI's 32%-46% into one series, and call it one episode, never a measured correlation or a reason VT offsets it.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 reservoir for claim 2, quotes rechecked at source (21 Feb 2023: the Midjourney images are not the product of human authorship; the text and the arrangement are protected); a registration decision, never a suggestion that Laura uses AI.
Wed 18 Nov: store: cite only the D.C. Circuit opinion (verified) until the Supreme Court's order list is read; the cert denial rests on a law firm's note.
Wed 18 Nov: store for claim 2: an author can bargain AI art off her own covers and interiors; a model clause, not a norm, never a claim about Laura's contracts.
Wed 18 Nov: store: a publisher's notice with no measured effect; serves no part beyond row 24's point.
Wed 18 Nov: store: drop the 1.7%-of-deposit comparison (the deposit is not licensing income) and never set the deal beside her publisher (H9-028); one nonfiction deal.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: use the fact sheet's 10,185 stocks (card Q1c, 30 Sep 2026), not a third-party 10,242, and never set VT's technology weights beside her career, which reads as the banned hedge.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 reservoir: its own critique (Viceira, Q1-005) and card Q33 say own risk lowers shares somewhat, so never not for fewer shares; say the IPS holds shares only with unpromised money (l.11), and 2023-25 is one episode, not proof of no correlation.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3's one figure (GOLDMINE 39); figures match NUMBERS 8u and 5 and supersede Q2a-025's 74.5%; in prose only about three-quarters smaller, at today's rates; the one-in-five pairing waits on row 15's base.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e and Table 3 reservoir; figures match NUMBERS 5 ($56,251, $17,087, $65,000; $40,000); it lands on the contribution only while the cut is under about three-quarters, so say that; nothing beyond the register.
Wed 18 Nov: store for claim 4: the trade's earlier structural shock, dated at source; essays, not data, and magazines also lost advertising to television.
Wed 18 Nov: store for claim 4: SEC filings, arithmetic checked (8.3%, 20%; S&P 2007 5.48% in the repo file); say stock images, not illustrators, and never the 2009 claim without the 2006-07 dates.
Wed 18 Nov: store for claim 2: publishing held while the low end moved, in a seller's memo written to raise money; row 16's squeezed educational fees cut the other way now.
Wed 18 Nov: store: the old escape route matching rows 7 and 11; a history site's narrative, colour only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e reservoir: say an AI shock lacks the second hit a recession tends to bring (falling yields, Q1-048), never milder or that 73.9% does not move (78.6% on the 13 Nov curve; it moves until 4 Jan 2027); 69.1% stays in NUMBERS 5, about three-quarters is 2.3's one figure.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e note 1 reservoir: case l.44-45 names advances, speaking, licensing and other ventures, so say advances are paid in quarters over years (Q127), never that the deposit comes mostly from contracts already signed, nor anything about her own contracts.

Wed 18 Nov: restates the two lists and CANON D9 for image models; its only-a-missed-deposit-changes-the-plan wording sits beside the banned only-two line, so the guard lives in Q109-033 and NUMBERS 8u.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 one-sentence candidate (riskier in degree, not in kind); fix bought before her income can be tested: most of each payment is bought with money she has, and the rest needs about a quarter of the 2028 deposit, the one date her income is tested.
